pois.name: Milwaukee City Hall
pois.blurb: Milwaukee City Hall is the seat of the municipal government of Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The Flemish Renaissance Revival building was completed in 1895 and still contains city offices and council facilities.

themeConnection.text: Milwaukee City Hall was completed in 1895 and remains the principal building for the city's mayor and municipal government.

pois.name: Ghent City Hall
pois.blurb: Ghent City Hall is the historic municipal hall of Ghent, Belgium. Its surviving complex includes fifteenth- and sixteenth-century buildings and continues to house official city administration and civic functions.

themeConnection.text: Ghent City Hall incorporates medieval and Renaissance sections and remains the working seat of Ghent's municipal government.

pois.name: Providence City Hall
pois.blurb: Providence City Hall is a historic city hall in Providence, Rhode Island. Completed in 1878, the building remains occupied by the mayor, city departments, and other core municipal functions.

themeConnection.text: Providence City Hall was completed in 1878 and continues to serve as the city's municipal headquarters.

pois.name: Hôtel de Ville de Paris
pois.blurb: The Hôtel de Ville (French: [otɛl də vil] ; French for 'City Hall') is the city hall of Paris, France, standing on the Place de l'Hôtel-de-Ville – Esplanade de la Libération in the 4th arrondissement.

themeConnection.text: Paris's Hôtel de Ville was rebuilt and completed in 1882 and remains the seat of the Mayor of Paris and city administration.

pois.name: Charleston City Hall
pois.blurb: Charleston City Hall is a historic municipal building in Charleston, South Carolina. Completed in 1804, it remains the official city hall and accommodates the offices and chambers of the city government.

themeConnection.text: Charleston City Hall was completed in 1804 and continues to house the municipal government of Charleston.

pois.name: Brussels Town Hall
pois.blurb: Brussels Town Hall is a Gothic building on the Grand Place and remains the town hall of the City of Brussels. It continues to provide the municipality's principal ceremonial and official civic functions.

themeConnection.text: Brussels Town Hall was built in the fifteenth century and remains the official municipal hall of the City of Brussels.

pois.name: Glasgow City Chambers
pois.blurb: Glasgow City Chambers is the headquarters of Glasgow City Council. Opened in 1888, the building remains the city's principal civic complex, with council chambers, offices, and continuing municipal use.

themeConnection.text: Glasgow City Chambers opened in 1888 and continue to house the city's elected council and municipal administration.

pois.name: Sheffield Town Hall
pois.blurb: Sheffield Town Hall is a municipal building in Sheffield, England. Completed in 1897, it continues to be used by Sheffield City Council for council meetings, civic administration, and official functions.

themeConnection.text: Sheffield Town Hall was completed in 1897 and continues to house Sheffield City Council's civic functions.

pois.name: Baltimore City Hall
pois.blurb: Baltimore City Hall is the official seat of government for the City of Baltimore. Its Second Empire building was completed in 1875 and still houses the mayor's office and city administration.

themeConnection.text: Baltimore City Hall, completed in 1875, continues to contain the offices of the mayor and Baltimore municipal government.

pois.name: Quebec City Hall
pois.blurb: Quebec City Hall is the city hall of Quebec City, Quebec. The historic building opened in 1896 and continues to serve as the seat of the mayor and the municipal government.

themeConnection.text: Quebec City Hall opened in 1896 and remains the official building of Quebec City's municipal administration.

pois.name: Cincinnati City Hall
pois.blurb: Cincinnati City Hall is the seat of the municipal government of Cincinnati, Ohio. The Richardsonian Romanesque building was completed in 1893 and continues to house city offices and council functions.

themeConnection.text: Cincinnati City Hall was completed in 1893 and remains the working seat of Cincinnati's city government.

pois.name: Luxembourg City Hall
pois.blurb: Luxembourg City Hall (French: Hôtel de ville de Luxembourg [otɛl də vil də lyksɑ̃buʁ]; Luxembourgish: Stadhaus Stad Lëtzebuerg) is the city hall of Luxembourg City, in southern Luxembourg.

themeConnection.text: Luxembourg City Hall dates from the nineteenth century and remains the seat of the municipal government of Luxembourg City.

pois.name: New Orleans City Hall
pois.blurb: New Orleans City Hall is the seat of the municipal government of New Orleans, Louisiana. The building was completed in 1853 and continues to provide official city offices and civic rooms.

themeConnection.text: The present New Orleans City Hall was completed in 1853 and remains the official municipal-government building.

pois.name: St. Louis City Hall
pois.blurb: St. Louis City Hall is the seat of government for the independent city of St. Louis, Missouri. Completed in 1893, it remains an active municipal building with city offices and council chambers.

themeConnection.text: St. Louis City Hall was completed in 1893 and still houses the mayor, city council, and municipal administration.

pois.name: Montreal City Hall
pois.blurb: Montreal City Hall is a historic building in Old Montreal and the seat of the municipal government. Completed in 1878, it continues to accommodate the mayor and important city-government functions.

themeConnection.text: Montreal City Hall was completed in 1878 and continues to house the mayor's office and municipal civic functions.

pois.name: Edinburgh City Chambers
pois.blurb: The City Chambers in Edinburgh are the headquarters of the City of Edinburgh Council. The complex includes historic eighteenth-century fabric and remains an active municipal building with council and administrative functions.

themeConnection.text: Edinburgh City Chambers originated in the eighteenth century and remain the headquarters of the City of Edinburgh Council.

pois.name: Antwerp City Hall
pois.blurb: The City Hall (Dutch: ) of Antwerp, Belgium, stands on the western side of that city's Grote Markt (main square).

themeConnection.text: Antwerp City Hall was completed in 1565 and continues to serve as the city's municipal hall.

pois.name: New York City Hall
pois.blurb: New York City Hall is the seat of New York City government, located at the center of City Hall Park in the Civic Center area of Lower Manhattan, between Broadway, Park Row, and Chambers Street.

themeConnection.text: Completed in 1812, New York City Hall remains the seat of the city's mayor and municipal government.

pois.name: Birmingham Council House
pois.blurb: The Council House is the seat of local government in Birmingham, England. Completed in 1879, it remains a working civic building containing council chambers, municipal offices, and official reception spaces.

themeConnection.text: Birmingham Council House was completed in 1879 and remains a working seat of Birmingham City Council.

pois.name: Guildhall
pois.blurb: Guildhall is a municipal building in the City of London, England. It is off Gresham and Basinghall streets, in the wards of Bassishaw and Cheap.

themeConnection.text: London's Guildhall is the historic municipal hall of the City of London and remains the headquarters of its civic corporation.

clue.text: In the early republic, this civic building became a stage for national mourning when Abraham Lincoln’s coffin lay in state beneath its grand rotunda. It is still the oldest American city hall carrying out its original governmental role, with a mayor’s office and council chambers in a formal, columned building set in a public park.

theme.title: Historic Working City Halls
theme.introduction: Stone towers, clocklit chambers, and civic squares still anchor the daily life of cities around the world.
theme.inclusionCriteria: Include a location only when every condition is met: (1) it is an individually named city hall, town hall, municipal hall, Rathaus, hôtel de ville, ayuntamiento, palazzo comunale, or clearly equivalent building; (2) the present building, or a continuously recognized predecessor occupying the same identifiable site, was completed, opened for civic use, or first established there on or before 31 December 1899; (3) the building still houses the government of its present-day city or incorporated municipality, including the mayor’s office, council chamber, municipal administration, or another official core civic function, on the date of play; (4) it occupies a fixed, individually mappable building or contiguous civic complex with a recognizable exterior or public entrance; (5) the site lies within the current administrative boundary of a present-day city or incorporated urban municipality; and (6) the location is identifiable by its official civic name rather than only by a surrounding square, district, palace, or administrative campus. The worldwide set should provide at least 35 plausible locations across many cities and countries.
